title: Rapid Onramp Ops: Blitzcard Prototype
summary: A compact, actionable operator-facing sales sheet designed for fast pilot qualification: pragmatic scripts, environment checklists, and a minimal canary/fallback decision tree to enable sellers and SEs to launch low-friction pilots in <2 weeks.
content: Why this exists: sellers repeatedly ask for a single-page bundle they can hand to platform engineers and SREs during a pilot kickoff. Existing decks are long; this is a riff on a one-shot operational blitzcard that pairs a short technical checklist with buyer-aware messaging.

Primary audience: platform engineers and integration architects evaluating Redwood for production inference — secondary audience is SEs and field sellers who need a rapid, defensible next step for pilots.
Core promise to the buyer: predictable latency and cost controls during pilot scale, with built-in, non-invasive fallback modes so the app stays online if peak load or throttling occurs.

One-liner scripts for the rep (30s): 
  - Platform engineer: 'We’ll run a 7–14 day pilot using a mirrored traffic route with a 10% live-sample funnel. We’ll measure p50/p95 latency, token cost per session, and functional quality thresholds — you keep full control of keys and network.'
  - Integration architect: 'We support in-VPC private deployments and can run a non-prod air-gapped trial if you need stricter egress controls.'

Pilot sizing heuristics (quick table):
  - Small pilot: 5k tokens/day, 1 model variant, synthetic load + 1 integration test
  - Medium pilot: 50k tokens/day, 2-3 model variants, traffic mirroring for 3 endpoints
  - Scale check: 250k+ tokens/day, dedicated pool suggested, recommend reserved capacity discussion

Must-have checklist for kickoff (ops-focused):
  - Network: outbound egress allowed to redwood-managed endpoints OR VPC peering confirmed
  - Auth: test API key and role with read-only telemetry access configured
  - Data: sanitized prompts only for pilot; PII gating agreed or pseudonymization in place
  - SLAs: define acceptable p95 latency and an escalated fallback window (e.g., 30s)
  - Observability: enable token-level tracing for first 48 hours

Canary and fallback patterns (decision guidance):
  - If p95 breach occurs and throughput still below threshold: enable aggressive batching profile (apply immediately)
  - If error spikes or model OOMs: fallback to lower-memory quantized variant with identical API surface
  - If regional capacity constraints: route to cross-region compatible model with degraded quality notice

Field rebuttals (short bullets):
  - Objection: 'We can’t risk inconsistent outputs.' Rebuttal: 'We pin model versions for the pilot and enable A/B rollouts with canary thresholds; if regressions appear we auto-fallback to the prior pinned version.'
  - Objection: 'Latency matters more than cost.' Rebuttal: 'We’ll provision a dedicated trial pool for the pilot window and instrument latency SLO alerts; cost controls remain visible but deprioritized for the test.'

Evidence snippets to share with buyer (links to internal benchmarks and quick graphs):
  - 95th percentile latency heatmap for typical consumer chat workload (link to internal dashboard)
  - Cost delta table: streaming + prefix cache vs naive single-request baseline
  - Case vignette: integration team reduced token spend by 24% with prefix caching during their 2-week pilot

Success criteria (mutual):
  - Technical: sustained p95 latency under agreed threshold for 72 consecutive hours while handling expected traffic shape
  - Business: end-to-end user flow demonstrates equivalent or improved UX and cost per session within target range
  - Ops: rollback/fallback exercised once and verified

Quick engineering handoff payload (what to attach to the pilot ticket):
  - API example calls + sample payloads (curl/snippet)
  - Suggested autoscaling thresholds and resource plan
  - Test plan for canary traffic mirroring

SE play notes (two minute prep):
  - Ask early: 'Are you ok with a mirrored 10% sample to start?' If no, propose a synthetic load test that mirrors production sequencing.
  - Bring up: keyspace caching (prefix/KV) as an easy first optimization that doesn’t change prompts.
  - Escalation: map to SRE contact, and confirm fallback route before the first scaled run.

Follow-up cadence for pilot: Day 0 kickoff note; Day 1 operational check; Day 3 deep telemetry review; Day 7 mini-retro; Day 14 fidelity & economics review. Outcome options: convert to dedicated pool, extend pilot with expanded traffic, or stop and rollback.

Open questions for product/ops teams (for iteration):
  - Could we ship a single click 'pilot bundle' that creates a mirrored route + pre-configured reserved trial pool?
  - What minimal additional telemetry hooks improve rep confidence without exposing raw prompt data?
Attachments implied in this doc: curl examples, a 1-page PDF summary for buyer, a small dashboard screenshot for p95/p50 trends (to be attached in repo).
